prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (call sign Juniper) is the region’s continuous intake, triage-support, dispatch, and coordination point under approved protocols; jurisdictions retain resource ownership and local-policy responsibility. It creates incident records, maintains a shared operational picture, preserves original caller reports alongside clarifications, and escalates readiness gaps. Call Taker Mara (call sign Larkspur) confirms and repeats location before medical details, captures symptoms, hazards, and access barriers, distinguishes observed facts from secondhand reports, and updates records before dispatch. She produces a Caller Location Correction Slip. Computer Aided Dispatch Console checks locations against address/map data and presents current incident details, priority, travel times, availability, and access constraints; staff verify data currency. Triage Supervisor (operational alias Copperfield) reviews uncertain, conflicting, deteriorating, severe, or escalation-worthy cases; directs focused clarification without delaying urgent response; assigns and documents priority by immediacy, care time-sensitivity, and deterioration risk. Immediate threats get highest available priority and prompt dispatch. Supervisor sends Pediatric Acuity Note, confirms response level against caller information, and refers unusual cases to Regional Medical Director when time permits. Regional Medical Director sets policy and may advise on unusual clinical resource needs, without dispatch authority. Data Quality Officer (alias Pebble) flags defects but cannot change priority; audits completeness, compliance, and recorded priority-change rationales, and sends Duplicate Incident Audit Memo. Ambulance Coordination Platform uses priority, requirements, unit status/capabilities, and constraints to present suitable units. Selection follows priority confirmation and weighs clinical need, travel time, vehicle/crew capability and readiness, and regional coverage. Radio Coordinator (alias Mistral) checks unit reachability and communicates instructions/priority changes over Regional Radio Network. Dispatch authorization follows regional approval rules; Shift Commander (alias Sundial) approves exceptions reducing coverage or requiring nonstandard response, and is notified of capacity conflicts. Dispatcher records authorized unit and conditions. Ambulance Unit 417 follows instructions and requests clarification if unsafe. Paramedic Crew reports material patient-condition changes and assesses/treats within scope. Emergency Department may provide capacity information; clinical triage follows protocols. Riverside Trauma Center is considered when needs and guidance support it. Hospital Liaison Desk confirms capabilities and pathways and produces Bedside Arrival Receipt on confirmed arrival. Fleet Maintenance Cell (alias Bluejay) reports unavailable/restricted vehicles and produces Battery Swap Voucher for authorized replacement. Shift Commander manages coordination, continuity, surge, conflicts, and readiness, not clinical authority. Readiness covers staffing, communications,

New part:
S113: The Radio Coordinator selects the appropriate talkgroup and confirms that it is available before transmitting.
S114: The dispatch transmission states the incident identifier, location, priority, response assignment, and any immediate hazard information.
S115: The Paramedic Crew acknowledges the assignment and repeats the location and priority for confirmation.
S116: The dispatcher corrects any discrepancy through a fresh transmission rather than relying on an unclear acknowledgment.
S117: If the assigned unit does not acknowledge promptly, the Radio Coordinator attempts contact again and alerts the dispatch supervisor.
S118: The North Gate Status Board and South Gate Status Board support routing decisions when access conditions are changing.
S119: Dispatchers state a confirmed gate or approach constraint explicitly and identify any uncertainty in the information.
S120: The controlled handoff occurs when the crew has acknowledged the assignment and the dispatch floor has confirmed the essential details.
S121: The Paramedic Crew reports any material conflict between the transmitted route and conditions observed in the field.
S122: The Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates destination information with the receiving Emergency Department when required.
S123: Radio Coordinator sends the Coverage Gap Bulletin when available ambulance coverage falls below the regional threshold.
S124: Juniper records the authorization time and the reason for selecting the assigned unit.
S125: Regional Dispatch Center maintains a regional coverage picture from current unit locations, crew reports, and readiness information.
S126: Ambulance Coordination Platform consolidates unit position and status so dispatchers can compare available coverage across the region.
S127: Computer Aided Dispatch Console presents staging options that account for response demand, travel time, and access constraints.
S128: Paramedic Crew reports when a unit is available, responding, on scene, transporting, or temporarily unavailable.
S129: Crews update their status promptly after a material change so dispatch decisions reflect the unit's actual condition.
S130: Regional Radio Network carries route instructions and crew acknowledgments between dispatch and field units.
S131: Mistral confirms approved route changes over the Regional Radio Network before a crew diverts.
S132: Bluejay verifies maintenance clearance before a unit returns to available status.
S133: Ambulance Unit 417 reports its position and operating status when it enters or leaves a staging area.
S134: A crew remains at its assigned staging point until dispatch confirms a new location or a direct response assignment.
S135: South Gate Status Board displays current access conditions for units approaching the southern entry.
S136: Sundial reviews the regional coverage picture before approving a staging move.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
